explain.say: Imagine you had mastered every subject at university, and you were bored. Doctor Faustus is. Christopher Marlowe wrote his play around 1590, about a scholar who sells his soul to the devil for twenty-four years of power. The panels follow him.

explain.say: Look at the third panel. Faustus signs the contract in his own blood, and the blood congeals, as if his body says no. When he asks Mephistopheles why he is out of hell, the devil answers: why, this is hell, nor am I out of it. What does the devil mean?

explain.say: Marlowe borrows from old morality plays like Everyman. See the board: a Good Angel urges repent, a Bad Angel urges go forward, and an Old Man pleads with him. Every time Faustus wavers, the devils frighten or distract him. Which voice would win you over?

explain.say: So what does he do with infinite power? Look at the fourth and fifth panels: pranks, conjuring tricks for emperors, and a vision of Helen of Troy. He says: was this the face that launched a thousand ships? Is that a grand use of power, or a waste?

explain.say: In his last hour he begs time to stop, and cries: I'll burn my books! Critics split. On the left, a warning about pride and damnation. On the right, the overreacher, a hero of boundless ambition. Brilliant. Challenge: what would you ask for, and what is your price?

faq.q: Why does Faustus sell his soul?
faq.a: He has exhausted ordinary learning and craves godlike knowledge, power, wealth and pleasure, so he trades his soul for twenty-four years of Mephistopheles' service.

faq.q: What are the Good and Bad Angels?
faq.a: Two figures from the morality-play tradition who appear at moments of choice: the Good Angel urges Faustus to repent, the Bad Angel urges him on to magic and pleasure.
asks: Good Angel and Bad Angel in Doctor Faustus

faq.a: He believes he is beyond forgiveness, he is frightened and distracted by the devils, and pride keeps him from turning back. Critics debate whether he could not repent or would not.

faq.q: What does Was this the face that launched a thousand ships mean?
faq.a: Faustus is greeting the spirit of Helen of Troy, whose beauty caused the Trojan War, when a thousand Greek ships sailed. The line is gorgeous, but Helen is only a spirit, an illusion.
asks: Helen of Troy speech in Doctor Faustus

faq.q: What are the A-text and B-text?
faq.a: The two early versions of the play, printed in 1604 and 1616. The B-text is longer, with extra comic scenes and changes, so editors choose between them.

facts: The A-text of Doctor Faustus was printed in 1604 and the B-text in 1616.
Marlowe was killed in Deptford in 1593, aged 29.
Marlowe's source was the English Faust Book, a translation of a German story.
